prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: Database column specification for orders table (language en).
Grid: 5 columns × 9 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Column" · longest unbreakable word 137px · one-line width 137px
  col 2: header "Type" · longest unbreakable word 99px · one-line width 210px
  col 3: header "Nullable" · longest unbreakable word 59px · one-line width 59px
  col 4: header "Default" · longest unbreakable word 161px · one-line width 161px
  col 5: header "Comment" · longest unbreakable word 93px · one-line width 577px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
This table cannot fit without splitting words at 360px. You MAY choose a total wider than 359px (the reader then scrolls horizontally), or squeeze and accept splits — a design decision.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

The image shows the table's content with every cell on one line, so you can read everything. Study it first.
1) Understand it: what is the table for, how will people read, scan and compare it, which columns play the same or similar role, which values must stay intact, which text may wrap naturally, and where existing row height could absorb wrapping.
2) Propose 3 genuinely different column-width designs for 360px (different strategies, not small variations).
Reply ONLY JSON: {"understanding":{"purpose":"","reading":"","groups":["columns that belong together and why"],"keep_intact":[""],"may_wrap":[""]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[int px per column, column 1 first],"idea":"one sentence"}]}

log.raw: {"understanding":{"purpose":"A reference spec of the orders table's columns — an engineering artifact read to answer 'what columns exist, what type, can it be null, what's the default, what does it mean'. It is consulted, not compared numerically; the reader jumps to a column name and then reads across that row.","reading":"Top-to-bottom scan of the Column column (identifiers are the index), then a rightward read of that row's Type / Nullable / Default, with Comment read only when needed. Cross-row comparison of Type values is secondary but real (repeated BIGINT UNSIGNED, TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE).","groups":["Column + Type form the identity pair — always read together and must never be broken mid-token","Nullable + Default form the constraint pair — both are short flag-like values, low information density, safe to keep narrow","Comment is prose, a separate register, and can absorb wrapping at line breaks"],"keep_intact":["column identifiers (order_reference, total_amount_cents, cancelled_at) — snake_case split across lines is misread as two columns","type tokens (BIGINT UNSIGNED, VARCHAR(32), TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE) — breaking at spaces is tolerable, breaking inside a word is not","default literals (CURRENT_TIMESTAMP) — a single token, must not split","Nullable YES/NO — 3 characters, never wrap"],"may_wrap":["Comment — free prose, wraps at word boundaries with no loss","Type — may wrap between its words (TIMESTAMP / WITH TIME ZONE) if words stay whole","Default — may wrap to two lines if the token itself stays intact"]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[140,80,44,46,49],"idea":"Squeeze everything inside the 360px frame: no horizontal scroll on a phone, at the cost of splitting identifiers, type tokens and defaults — accept it because on a narrow screen the row still reads as one visual unit."},{"name":"B","widths":[158,231,80,182,200],"idea":"One modest scroll: give Column, Type, Nullable and Default exactly their one-line widths so every code-like value stays whole, and let only Comment wrap to a few lines."},{"name":"C","widths":[158,231,80,182,598],"idea":"Zero compromise on fidelity: every cell on one line including the full comments, so the table behaves like a single wide reference sheet the reader scrolls across deliberately."}]}
